mara: quick FYI — while onboarding omen-3b-v2 int4, I hit a weird divergence that only shows up when we prime with sparse 'meta' tokens (chunk markers).

mara: reproduction summary: quant int4 + streaming prefill, context_len=32768, prefix length ~150 with frequent ‘<seg>’ markers. float16 baseline OK. int4 emits correct tokens until ~token 1024, then generation drifts.

mara: logs/snippet:
```
cmd: ./eval-runner --model omen-3b-v2 --quant int4 --prompt-file priming_sparse.txt --streaming true --max-tokens 2048
first mismatch at token_idx=1024
ref: "the committee decided to..."
out: "the commitee desided to..."
KL spike at step=1024: 14.2 -> 26.9
KV-cache entries look good length-wise but cosine sim of cached keys drops sharply after position 1024
```

devon: interesting. does it reproduce if you remove the chunk markers or compress them (i.e., fewer special tokens)?

mara: yep — when I replace all <seg> with plain spaces, int4 matches float16 across whole window. if I keep markers but move them earlier in the prefix it still fails. looks position-sensitive.

priya: possible rotary/RoPE interaction? markers change tokenization and effective absolute positions; int4 scaling of RoPE magnets might be sensitive to fractional interpolation (we do per-head scaling in the kernel).

mara: that's our suspicion. also tried running with "disable_rope_scaling=true" and mismatch goes away (but obviously different generation quality).

eval-runner: queued a deterministic run comparing (float16, int8, int4) with three priming variants: original, markers->spaces, markers-bunched. Will post results (run id: run-20240506-872).

devon: can you paste the exact token ids around the boundary? trying to check whether tokenization introduces multi-byte tokens causing off-by-one in offsets.

mara: snippet of tokens near boundary:
```
... 1008: 4223 ("the")
1009: 1901 ("committee")
1010: 2 ("<seg>")
1011: 137 ("decided")
1012: 45 (",")
1013: ...
```

mara: note the marker token id=2 is a very low id (like BOS-ish). maybe our prefix remapping logic collapses positions for low ids?

priya: low-id tokens shouldn't matter for RoPE itself, but if kernel uses token->position packing for caching (we pack groups for int4 byte alignment), an alignment shift could offset KV indexing by a few columns. That would explain a sudden cosine drop when retrieving keys for positions >= 1024 (one aligned block boundary).

priya: action items I propose:
- reproduce with simplified tokenizer (no low-id special tokens)
- run with "dump-kv-raw=true" to inspect actual key vectors bytes at boundary (int4 packing view)
- run identical test on cpu/fp16 to confirm it's quantization kernel-only
- try toggling continuous batching vs single stream (to rule out batching-induced prefix offset)

mara: did a quick "dump-kv-raw" and here's excerpt (hex bytes per slot truncated):
```
pos 1018: keys_hex= 0a f3 9c ...
pos 1019: keys_hex= 0a f3 9c ...
pos 1020: keys_hex= 0b e2 8f ...  <-- jump
```

mara: see that jump at 1020 -> aligns with where mismatch begins.

devon: that strongly suggests packing/stride bug. the int4 packer increments an internal write pointer every N tokens — could be overflow at 1024 because of 256-byte block boundary (just guessing).

priya: there's also RoPE scaling code path that re-centers rotary frequencies for very long positions (we apply a piecewise scale when pos>max_fast_rope). maybe packer + scale interplay causes truncation.

mara: for immediate mitigation, we can add a prefill transform to collapse consecutive low-id markers into a single token in the tokenizer layer (cheap hack) and push a hotfix to dedicated pools. Diff suggestion below:
```diff
- raw_prefix = tokens_from_prompt(p)
- packed_prefix = pack_for_kv(raw_prefix)
+ raw_prefix = collapse_markers(tokens_from_prompt(p))  # collapse runs of <seg>
+ packed_prefix = pack_for_kv(raw_prefix)
```

eval-runner: run-20240506-872 finished. TL;DR:
- float16 baseline: no divergence
- int8: tiny drift ~1e-3 KL at 1200, recovers
- int4 baseline (original priming): divergence at 1024 consistent
- int4 with marker-collapse: no divergence
- int4 with disable_rope_scaling: no divergence but slightly worse token probs overall

mara: I've opened ML-2319 with repro steps and attached run logs + dump-kv-raw. assigning to @devon for kernel dive.

devon: ack. I'll add a unit test to the int4 packer to stress chunk boundaries (align at 1024, 2048, 4096) and run CI on a dedicated GPU.

priya: also tagging eng-runtime to review the RoPE long-pos fallback math. @ops-bot can you open ops ticket for a canary config change (collapse markers) on a small dedicated pool?

ops-bot: ops ticket opened: OPS-665 (canary marker-collapse for dedicated-qa). Scheduled 2024-05-08 02:00 UTC.

mara: thanks everyone. will keep thread updated with eval artifacts. if kernel fix takes longer, marker-collapse is safe short-term mitigation. :white_check_mark:

priya: nice find. feels like a subtle interaction of packing + RoPE scaling. good catch on the low-id marker hypothesis.

mara: filing a quick doc note about this pattern for future onboarding checks (sparse priming + int4).
